transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I, uh… I came in because flying has become… really hard. Even just thinking about getting on a plane scares me badly. I know it doesn’t really make sense, but my body reacts like the plane is going to fall.
Is your fear of flying something that only happens in specific situations, or do you also feel anxious in other circumstances, like in crowds or when you're away from home?
It’s mostly that specific thing… flying. Even just the thought of getting on a plane now scares me badly. I know it doesn’t really make sense, but I feel like it’s going to fall.
When you feel this fear of flying, do you also experience symptoms like a racing heart, sweating, trembling, or feeling like you can’t breathe?

Yes… pretty much right away. Even if it’s just an email about a rural shift that would mean flying, my heart starts pounding, my hands get sweaty, and I feel like I can’t breathe. I usually have to close the message.
Outside of flying or thinking about flying, do you ever have these anxiety attacks in other situations, like in crowds, while driving, or even when you're at home resting?
No… not really. It’s the airplane thing. Even the thought of getting on one… I know it sounds irrational, but my body just reacts like the plane is going to fall.
Does the thought of flying ever lead you to avoid making travel plans or going to places that would require you to fly?

Yes. I’ve canceled clinic coverage, skipped medical meetings… and I’ve put off seeing my family in Honduras. If it means going to the airport, I just… I can’t do it unless someone is with me and I’m basically shaking the whole time.
Have you ever felt this level of fear about anything else, or is this the only situation that makes you feel this way?
It’s really just flying. The thought of getting on an airplane… it scares me so much. I know it doesn’t make sense, but my body feels like the plane is going to fall.
How long have you felt this intense fear of flying? Has it been going on for months or even years?
About seven months now… it started after that rough small-plane flight, around the time I lost my clinic job. Since then it’s just… stayed with me.
When you think about flying, do you go out of your way to avoid it completely, or do you sometimes try to tolerate it with a lot of distress?

I mostly avoid it. I’ve canceled coverage and skipped meetings because of it… and I keep putting off visiting my family in Honduras. If I do even get near the airport, I’m shaking and I need someone with me.
Have you ever worried that you might have another panic attack in a place where it would be hard to get help or escape, like on an airplane, in a crowd, or in a car?
I’m not sure… I don’t think it’s crowds or cars like that. It’s mostly the plane itself, being stuck up there. I haven’t really thought of it as worrying about panic attacks.
Have you ever experienced sudden episodes of intense fear or discomfort that reached a peak within minutes, even when you weren’t thinking about flying?
Not really… I mean, I can’t think of times like that when flying wasn’t involved. If it’s happened, I haven’t noticed it that way.
Have you ever had sudden episodes of intense fear or discomfort that came out of nowhere, even when you weren’t thinking about flying or being on a plane?
No… I don’t think so. Not out of nowhere. I haven’t really noticed anything like that unless it’s connected to flying.
